Netlify runs on Linux which is case-sensitive, but Mac/Windows aren't — so a folder called Images won't match images in your code. Check these things: 1. Check your folder names exactly Your HTML references: images/logo.png images/passes/Screenshot... Open your project folder and make sure it's named exactly images (all lowercase) and the subfolder is exactly passes (all lowercase). If it's Images or Passes with a capital letter, rename them to lowercase. 2. Check the images folder was actually uploaded On your Netlify dashboard, go to Deploys → click your latest deploy → Browse deploy. This lets you browse every file Netlify received. Check if the images folder is there with the passes subfolder inside it. 3. File names with spaces Your pass photos have spaces in the names (e.g. Screenshot 2026-05-17 at 12.29.45.png). These usually work fine but if they're still not showing after fixing the above, you may need to rename them without spaces — though that's a bigger job so try the folder name fix first. The most likely fix is just renaming Images → images and Passes → passes on your computer, then re-uploading to Netlify. The fix is to compress them first. Here's the easiest way on Mac: Compress all images at once on Mac: Open the passes folder Select all photos (Cmd + A) Right-click → Quick Actions → Convert Image Choose JPEG, size Small It'll create compressed copies — use those instead This should bring each photo from ~3MB down to ~100KB, making the whole folder around 10MB instead of 300MB. Or use a free website: Go to tinypng.com Drag all your photos in (it does batches) Download the compressed versions Use those in your passes folder Once the images are smaller, push to GitHub and Netlify will update automatically. The images will also load much faster on the website for visitors, so this is worth doing anyway! 1779105834497_image.png HOW DO I GET RIDE OF OTHER ONES 18 May I can see the problem — the Mac has created compressed copies (the ones showing "Screenshot 2026-0...ll.jpeg" in blue) alongside the original PNG files. You need to delete the originals and keep only the new JPEGs. Here's how: Click on any file in the folder Press Cmd + A to select all Now click "Kind" at the top to sort by file type — this groups PNGs together and JPEGs together Click the first PNG, scroll to the last PNG, hold Shift and click the last PNG to select all PNGs Press Cmd + Delete to move them to the bin Then you'll only have the smaller JPEG versions left. Then push to GitHub again. Or even easier — sort by name: In Finder, go to View → Show View Options (Cmd + J) Sort by Kind All the PNGs will group together at the bottom Select them all and delete 1779127008322_image.png how do i put the pictures 18 May The site is looking great! 🎉 The hero background is black because the pass photos still aren't in GitHub. Stripe — how to add online payment

If your site is on Vercel and likely built with Next.js, Stripe is a very good option.

You’ve basically got 2 main ways:

Option 1 — Easiest: Stripe Payment Links

Best if you want something quick without much coding.

How it works

You create payment links in Stripe for things like:

  • Manual lesson – £36

  • Automatic lesson – £38

  • 10-hour block

  • Assessment lesson

  • Booking deposit

Then your website buttons send users to the Stripe payment page.

Pros

  • fast

  • simple

  • secure

  • no heavy development

Cons

  • less flexible

  • harder to tie payment directly to a chosen calendar slot unless you build extra logic

Good for

If you just want:
“Book request now, pay now”

Option 2 — Better: Stripe Checkout integrated into your site

Best if you want a proper booking system.

Flow

  1. User chooses lesson type/date/time

  2. Clicks Continue to payment

  3. Your site creates a Stripe Checkout Session

  4. User pays

  5. Stripe sends success webhook

  6. Your system saves the booking and sends confirmation

Recommended setup for SAR

I’d suggest:

For single lessons

Take:

  • either full payment

  • or a £10–£20 deposit

For block bookings

Take:

  • full payment

  • or a partial deposit, then follow up manually

For test day bookings

Take:

  • full payment or a non-refundable deposit

That will reduce no-shows.

Basic Stripe integration steps

1) Create a Stripe account

Go to Stripe and set up:

  • business details

  • bank account

  • products/prices

2) Create products in Stripe

Examples:

  • Manual Lesson – 1 Hour – £36

  • Automatic Lesson – 1 Hour – £38

  • Refresher Lesson – from £38

  • Assessment Lesson – £38

  • Test Day Booking – custom price

  • Booking Deposit – £10 or £20

3) Install Stripe in your project

If you are using Next.js:

Bash
npm install stripe

4) Create an API route for checkout

Example idea:

JavaScript
// /api/create-checkout-session
import Stripe from "stripe";

const stripe = new Stripe(process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY);

export default async function handler(req, res) {
  if (req.method !== "POST") return res.status(405).end();

  const { lessonName, amount, bookingData } = req.body;

  const session = await stripe.checkout.sessions.create({
    payment_method_types: ["card"],
    mode: "payment",
    line_items: [
      {
        price_data: {
          currency: "gbp",
          product_data: {
            name: lessonName,
          },
          unit_amount: amount, // in pence
        },
        quantity: 1,
      },
    ],
    success_url: `${req.headers.origin}/success`,
    cancel_url: `${req.headers.origin}/cancel`,
    metadata: {
      learnerName: bookingData.name,
      phone: bookingData.phone,
      date: bookingData.date,
      time: bookingData.time,
      lessonType: bookingData.lessonType,
    },
  });

  res.status(200).json({ url: session.url });
}

5) Send user to Stripe Checkout

Frontend example:

JavaScript
const handlePayment = async () => {
  const res = await fetch("/api/create-checkout-session", {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      lessonName: "Automatic Driving Lesson",
      amount: 3800,
      bookingData: {
        name: "John Smith",
        phone: "07123456789",
        date: "2026-05-25",
        time: "15:00",
        lessonType: "Automatic",
      },
    }),
  });

  const data = await res.json();
  window.location.href = data.url;
};

6) Add Stripe webhook

This is important.

Use a webhook so when payment succeeds:

  • save booking in database

  • mark it as paid

  • send confirmation email

  • optionally send WhatsApp/admin notification

Typical event:

  • checkout.session.completed

7) Save booking in database

You’ll likely want a table like:

bookings

  • id

  • name

  • email

  • phone

  • lesson_type

  • transmission

  • duration

  • location

  • price

  • date

  • time

  • payment_status

  • stripe_session_id

  • created_at

If you’re using Supabase already, that’s perfect.

Best tech setup for your case

Since you’ve worked with Supabase before, I’d do:

  • Frontend: Next.js / Vercel

  • Database: Supabase

  • Payments: Stripe Checkout

  • Availability / bookings: custom booking form or calendar

  • Automation: Stripe webhook + confirmation email

If you are using Cal.com / embedded calendar

From the screenshots, it looks a bit like an embedded booking tool.

If that’s the case, you have 2 routes:

Route A — Keep calendar embed, improve branding

  • rename event type to SAR Driving School

  • remove instructor name if possible

  • remove video wording

  • update description

  • add Stripe after booking or before confirmation

Route B — Better long term

Build your own booking flow on your website:

  • lesson selection

  • calendar availability

  • Stripe payment

  • confirmation

That gives you much more control and looks more professional.

My recommendation for SAR specifically

Best version:

A simple 3-part booking page:

Section 1

Choose your lesson

  • manual

  • automatic

  • refresher

  • assessment

Section 2

Choose your date & time

  • show available slots

Section 3

Secure your booking

  • pay deposit or full payment with Stripe

Then:

  • confirmation page

  • automatic email/text

  • admin notification

Your index.html is mostly fine, but there are 2 issues I’d fix.

1) Mobile background disappeared because only the slide has the image

Your code uses:

JavaScript
div.style.backgroundImage = "url('images/toyotacorollasarpic.png')";

That is fine only if this file exists exactly:

images/toyotacorollasarpic.png

Check in Terminal:

Bash
cd Desktop/sarwebsite
ls images/

If the file name is different, rename it:

Bash
mv "images/OLD-FILE-NAME.png" "images/toyotacorollasarpic.png"

2) Cleaner fix for your mobile hero

Replace this whole part in your JavaScript:

JavaScript
const isMobile = window.innerWidth <= 768;

if (isMobile) {
  div.style.backgroundImage = "url('images/toyotacorollasarpic.png')";
} else {
  div.style.backgroundImage = `url('images/websitepictures/${photos[idx]}')`;
}

With this:

JavaScript
div.style.backgroundImage = `url('images/websitepictures/${photos[idx]}')`;

Then add this CSS inside your <style> block:

CSS
@media (max-width: 768px) {
  .hero {
    position: relative;
    min-height: 650px;
    padding: 80px 1.25rem 60px;
    overflow: hidden;
  }

  .hero::before {
    content: "";
    position: absolute;
    inset: 0;
    background: url('images/toyotacorollasarpic.png') center/cover no-repeat;
    z-index: 0;
  }

  .hero-slideshow {
    display: none !important;
  }

  .hero-overlay {
    position: absolute;
    inset: 0;
    z-index: 1;
    background: rgba(0,0,0,0.68);
  }

  .hero-inner {
    position: relative;
    z-index: 2;
  }

  .hero h1 {
    font-size: 2.15rem;
    line-height: 1.15;
  }

  .hero p {
    font-size: 1rem;
    line-height: 1.6;
  }

  .hero-buttons {
    flex-direction: column;
    gap: 0.8rem;
  }

  .btn-primary,
  .btn-secondary {
    width: 100%;
    text-align: center;
  }

  .hero-stats {
    grid-template-columns: 1fr;
    gap: 0.75rem;
  }

  .tab-cards {
    flex-direction: column;
  }

  .tab-card {
    width: 100% !important;
    min-width: unset !important;
  }
}

This is better because:

  • desktop still uses your rotating pass photos

  • mobile uses the Toyota SAR car as a fixed background

  • no JavaScript mobile detection needed

  • less chance of the image disappearing

Then push it

Bash
cd Desktop/sarwebsite
git add .
git commit -m "Fix mobile homepage background"
git push

<!DOCTYPE html>

  <style>
    /* MOBILE NAV FIX */
    @media (max-width: 768px) {
      .hamburger {
        display: flex !important;
        flex-direction: column;
        justify-content: center;
        gap: 5px;
        cursor: pointer;
        padding: 8px;
        background: none;
        border: none;
        z-index: 201;
      }

      .hamburger span {
        display: block;
        width: 24px;
        height: 2px;
        background: #111111;
        border-radius: 2px;
        transition: all 0.3s ease;

      .hamburger.open span:nth-child(1) { transform: translateY(7px) rotate(45deg); }
      .hamburger.open span:nth-child(2) { opacity: 0; }
      .hamburger.open span:nth-child(3) { transform: translateY(-7px) rotate(-45deg); }

      nav ul {
        display: none !important;

        left: 0;

        background: #ffffff;

        display: block;

      .nav-inner {
        position: relative;
        height: 70px;
      }
    }

4) Add this JavaScript

Put this in your bottom <script> section, underneath the hamburger code:

JavaScript
const lessonCards = document.querySelectorAll('.lesson-choice-card');
const selectedLessonText = document.getElementById('selectedLesson');

lessonCards.forEach(function(card) {
  card.addEventListener('mouseenter', function() {
    lessonCards.forEach(c => c.classList.remove('active'));
    card.classList.add('active');

    if (selectedLessonText) {
      selectedLessonText.textContent = card.dataset.lesson;
    }
  });

  card.addEventListener('click', function() {
    lessonCards.forEach(c => c.classList.remove('active'));
    card.classList.add('active');

    if (selectedLessonText) {
      selectedLessonText.textContent = card.dataset.lesson;
    }

    document.getElementById('my-cal-inline-driving-lesson').scrollIntoView({
      behavior: 'smooth',
      block: 'start'
    });
  });
});

Now whichever card your cursor is on will turn red, and clicking it will scroll the user down to the calendar.

        url("images/lessons-bg.png") center/cover no-repeat;

  <script>
    const hamburger = document.getElementById('hamburger');
    const navMenu = document.getElementById('nav-menu');

    hamburger.addEventListener('click', function() {
      hamburger.classList.toggle('open');
      navMenu.classList.toggle('open');
    });

    navMenu.querySelectorAll('a').forEach(function(link) {
      link.addEventListener('click', function() {
        hamburger.classList.remove('open');
        navMenu.classList.remove('open');
      });
    });

    function showTab(tab, btn) {
      document.querySelectorAll('.tab-content').forEach(function(content) {
        content.classList.remove('active');
      });

      document.querySelectorAll('.tab-btn').forEach(function(button) {
        button.classList.remove('active');
      });

      document.getElementById(tab).classList.add('active');
      btn.classList.add('active');
    }
  </script>
